title: Jia Xian's triangle of binomial numbers
summary: Chinese mathematician Jia Xian used the triangular array of binomial coefficients in the 11th century; Yang Hui defined it in the 13th. Indian and Persian scholars knew it too.
why: A basic tool of algebra, combinatorics and probability.

unsung.contribution: Used and described the triangle of binomial coefficients centuries before Blaise Pascal.
unsung.recognition: In much of the West it is named after Pascal, though mathematicians in India, Persia and China studied it centuries earlier.
